Q1: Activation verification of PR #7207 says `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED` should default to off. #7029 and #7272 deliberately made the stable-release switches default to on. Which should the pipeline do?
Choices:
A. Keep the default on and change no release behaviour. Add one `agents.d/` fragment and a changelog fragment saying that `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED` defaults to on on purpose, as the #7272 fragment says for `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED`. The fragment would also say that activation verification should not report this as a gap, so it stops filing this issue. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Keep the default on, change no files, and close this issue as not planned.
C. Do what the issue asks. In both release jobs, default `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED` to `false` in `env:` and in the `${STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED:-...}` script fallback, in `mark-stable.yml` and `test-and-mark-stable.yml`. Update the switch contract tests (`tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py`, `tests/test_release_manifest_workflow_contract.py`), README.md:242-243 and the workflow comments. Stable releases stop until an operator sets `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED=true`, which brings back the stall that #7029 fixed.
   **Note:** C contradicts #7029 and #7272, so `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` would still default to on. If you choose C, say whether that switch should also become default-off. Otherwise the planner will change only `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED`.
